findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric or out-of-range input
findings.failure_mode: malformed input (empty lines, whitespace-only lines, negative numbers, floats, or non-digit strings) causes a panic that aborts the entire task/thread instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: replace unwrap() with map_err to return a typed ParseError; change return type to Result<Vec<u32>, ParseError> or use an enum with a Parse variant

findings.problem: input.lines() has no static upper bound on iterations; untrusted input can cause arbitrary loop iterations
findings.failure_mode: an attacker or misconfigured client can supply a file with millions of lines, consuming unbounded CPU and memory during iteration
findings.fix: accept a max_items parameter; iterate with take(max_items) or enumerate with a len check that returns an error at the cap; the loop then has a provable static bound

findings.problem: external string input is parsed without any boundary validation; no input length limit, no character validation before parsing
findings.failure_mode: unbounded string input bypasses all safety checks before reaching the hot path; the function accepts any &str with no preconditions documented or enforced
findings.fix: add a max input length check before iterating; validate characters or accept a validated type; return Result with explicit error variants for InvalidInput, TooManyItems, ParseError, and Resource

findings.problem: every call allocates a new Vec<u32> on the heap with no allocation budget, no try_reserve, and no capacity hint
findings.failure_mode: hot-path calls cause unbounded heap churn; allocation failures return OOM panics via collect() rather than typed resource errors; no way to bound memory use per invocation
findings.fix: accept a pre-allocated Vec<&mut Vec<u32>> or use a try_reserve pattern with max_items; declare the allocation budget explicitly; return typed resource errors on allocation failure

findings.problem: unwrap() is a direct panic path in production-reachable code with no surrounding proof or waiver
findings.failure_mode: any line that is empty, whitespace, or non-numeric triggers a panic; there are no tests, proofs, or waivers demonstrating this path is unreachable in the deployment environment
findings.fix: use Result propagation with map_err; if the function is intended to be infallible for a validated domain, document and prove the invariant at the caller boundary instead of wrapping unwrap inside a pub fn

findings.problem: function is only 6 lines but lacks any type-level invariants, error type, or documented preconditions; the pub fn signature is too permissive for its actual safety requirements
findings.failure_mode: callers have no compile-time guarantee about input validity; the function signature lies about what it accepts
findings.fix: add a validated input type or error enum; document preconditions on the pub fn signature with #[doc] and invariant comments

findings.problem: no rust-toolchain.toml exists; no pinned nightly or stable toolchain; clippy would flag unwrap_used, panic_in_result_fn, and similar
findings.failure_mode: unpredictable compiler behavior across toolchain versions; no automated gate catches the forbidden constructs before merge
findings.fix: add a rust-toolchain.toml with a pinned dated nightly or stable channel; run cargo clippy with -D warnings in CI

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for parse_scores; no latency or throughput measurements
no profiler evidence (perf stat, cargo llvm-ir, or cargo asm) for the hot path shape
no tests exist for any input class (valid, empty, malformed, oversized)
no rust-toolchain.toml for pinned toolchain policy
no second-ring evidence (assembly/IR inspection, mechanical empathy tools)
no bounded-input tests proving the max_items fix works
residual_risk: static review only; this crate has no tests, no benchmarks, no CI gate, and no toolchain pin. The three BLOCKER violations (unwrap panic, unbounded loop, unbounded allocation) are clearly visible in the 6-line source but cannot be validated with command evidence. The function as written will panic on any malformed input and allocate unbounded memory per call.
